rows.subtopic: Trigonometric Ratios of an Acute Angle
rows.stem: If \(\sin A = \dfrac{2}{3}\), then value of \(\cot A\) is :
rows.solution:
\(\cos A = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2 A} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{4}{9}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\), taking A as an acute angle.

\(\cot A = \dfrac{\cos A}{\sin A} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}/3}{2/3} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\), which is option (A) \(\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\).

rows.stem: Which of the following is not probability of an event ?
rows.solution:
The probability of an event always lies between 0 and 1. The value 0.89 qualifies, \(52\% = 0.52\) qualifies, and \(\dfrac{1}{13}\% = \dfrac{1}{1300}\) also qualifies.

But \(\dfrac{1}{0.89} = \dfrac{100}{89} > 1\), so it cannot be a probability. This is option (D) \(\dfrac{1}{0.89}\).

rows.subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
rows.stem: If the sum and the product of zeroes of a quadratic polynomial are \(2\sqrt{3}\) and 3 respectively, then a quadratic polynomial is :
rows.solution:
A quadratic polynomial with sum of zeroes S and product P is \(x^2 - Sx + P\). Here that is \(x^2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,x + 3\).

\(x^2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,x + 3 = \left(x - \sqrt{3}\right)^2\), which is option (B) \(\left(x - \sqrt{3}\right)^2\).

rows.stem: \(n\)th term of an A.P. is \(7n + 4\). The common difference is :
Diagonals AC and BD of a trapezium ABCD intersect at O, where \(AB \parallel DC\). If \(\dfrac{DO}{OB} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), then show that AB = 2CD
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - trapezium ABCD with AB at the bottom, DC at the top and diagonals AC and BD crossing at O; the stem states every fact used (AB parallel to DC, DO/OB = 1/2). Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
In triangles OAB and OCD: \(\angle OAB = \angle OCD\) (alternate angles, since \(AB \parallel DC\)) and \(\angle AOB = \angle COD\) (vertically opposite angles). So \(\Delta OAB \sim \Delta OCD\) (AA similarity).

Corresponding sides are proportional: \(\dfrac{OD}{OB} = \dfrac{CD}{AB}\).

Since \(\dfrac{OD}{OB} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(\dfrac{CD}{AB} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), that is \(AB = 2CD\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: In a chemistry lab, there is some quantity of 50% acid solution and some quantity of 25% acid solution. How much of each should be mixed to make 10 litres of 40% acid solution ?
rows.solution:
Let x litres of the 50% solution and y litres of the 25% solution be mixed.

Total volume: \(x + y = 10\) ... (i)

Acid content: \(\dfrac{50}{100}x + \dfrac{25}{100}y = \dfrac{40}{100} \times 10\), that is \(2x + y = 16\) ... (ii)

Subtracting (i) from (ii): \(x = 6\), and then \(y = 4\).

Check: \(0.5 \times 6 + 0.25 \times 4 = 3 + 1 = 4\) litres of acid in 10 litres, which is 40%.

So 6 litres of the 50% solution and 4 litres of the 25% solution should be mixed.

rows.subtopic: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: A wooden toy is made by scooping out a hemisphere of same radius as of cylinder, from each end of a wooden solid cylinder. If the height of the cylinder is 20 cm and its base is of radius 7 cm, find the total surface area of the toy.
rows.solution:
The toy's surface is the curved surface of the cylinder plus the two scooped hemispherical surfaces, with \(r = 7\) cm and \(h = 20\) cm.

Total surface area \(= 2\pi rh + 2 \times 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi rh + 4\pi r^2\)

\(= 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 20 + 4 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 880 + 616 = 1496\) cm\(^2\).

rows.stem:
From the top of a building 60 m high, the angles of depression of the top and bottom of the vertical lamp post are observed to be \(30^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\) respectively.

(i) Find the horizontal distance between the building and the lamp post.

(ii) Find the distance between the tops of the building and the lamp post.
rows.solution:
Let AB be the building (60 m) and CD the lamp post of height h m, with A and C on the ground, \(AC = x\) m. The horizontal through B makes angles of depression \(30^\circ\) with BD and \(60^\circ\) with BC, so the angle of elevation of B from C is \(60^\circ\).

(i) In right triangle BAC: \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{AC}\), so \(\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{60}{x}\) and \(x = \dfrac{60}{\sqrt{3}} = 20\sqrt{3}\) m.

The horizontal distance between the building and the lamp post is \(20\sqrt{3}\) m \(\approx 34.64\) m.

(ii) Draw DE perpendicular to AB, so that \(DE = AC = 20\sqrt{3}\) m and \(\angle BDE = 30^\circ\). In right triangle BED:

\(\cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{DE}{BD}\), so \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \dfrac{20\sqrt{3}}{BD}\) and \(BD = \dfrac{2 \times 20\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = 40\) m.

The distance between the tops of the building and the lamp post is 40 m. (Also \(BE = DE \tan 30^\circ = 20\) m, so the lamp post is \(60 - 20 = 40\) m high.)

rows.subtopic: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: A vessel is in the form of a hollow hemisphere mounted by a hollow cylinder. The diameter of the hemisphere is 14 cm and the total height of the vessel is 13 cm. Find the inner surface area and the volume of the vessel.
rows.solution:
Radius of the hemisphere \(r = \dfrac{14}{2} = 7\) cm. Height of the cylindrical part \(h = 13 - 7 = 6\) cm.

Inner surface area \(= 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh = 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 + 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 6 = 308 + 264 = 572\) cm\(^2\).

Volume \(= \dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3 + \pi r^2 h = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 \times 7 + \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 \times 6\)

\(= \dfrac{2156}{3} + 924 = \dfrac{4928}{3} \approx 1642.67\) cm\(^3\).

The inner surface area is 572 cm\(^2\) and the volume is \(\dfrac{4928}{3}\) cm\(^3\), about 1642.67 cm\(^3\).
